Subject: Network triage notes — initial findings

Quick summary from the triage:
- Observed increased TCP retransmits and out-of-order frames in the pcap Elaine provided.
- Path trace (attached path-trace-20280830.png) shows asymmetric routing: customer egress -> our edge -> traffic returning via a different peering edge that applies a new stateful firewall cluster.
- The cloud FW cluster recently had a config push that enabled aggressive stateful reassembly for large TCP segments. We see evidence of fragmented packets being queued for reassembly causing head-of-line blocking; this increases per-request latency and triggers proxy timeouts -> 502/504 back to client.

Immediate mitigations applied at 09:20 PDT (temporary):
1) Applied path-based bypass for BrightForge subnet across the affected firewall cluster (bypass stateful reassembly).
2) Applied PMTU clamp to 1400 on the egress interface serving the peering to BrightForge (reduces fragmentation).
3) Temporarily shifted a percentage of traffic to an alternate peering that uses the older firewall cluster.

Result: p95 improved from ~820ms -> ~200ms and 5xx dropped from ~10% -> ~0.6% within ~6 minutes of changes. Full metrics in attached runbook.

Next steps (action items):
- Engineering to revert the aggressive reassembly config or make it non-applicable for VPC peering traffic (Vanessa + Infra).
- Network to coordinate a permanent routing change to avoid asymmetric peering for this account (Network + Cloud Partners).
- CS to draft customer comms and credit proposal (Marissa).
- Post-incident RCA and test plan to prevent future MTU fragmentation regressions (Soojin).

Attachments: path-trace-20280830.png

Vanessa Ortiz
Network Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec brief: BrightForge production disruption — MTU / firewall reassembly induced latency spike

Team — brief summary for execs and next steps (TL;DR at top).

Impact: BrightForge observed p99 inference latency climb to ~1.8s and ~10% 5xx on their checkout path for ~25 minutes on 2028-08-30 starting ~07:58 PDT. Estimated revenue impact: ~$120k during the window. Customer is asking for credits and executive engagement.

Root cause (initial): New stateful reassembly config on one firewall cluster combined with an asymmetric peering path caused fragmented packets to be queued/reassembled at the firewall. This produced head-of-line blocking and caused our proxy timeouts to return 502/504 downstream. There was also an MTU mismatch on the peering path.

What we did (completed):
- Applied targeted bypass of stateful reassembly for BrightForge's subnet (09:20 PDT).
- Set PMTU clamp to 1400 on egress for the peering interface.
- Shifted traffic to alternate peering edges temporarily.
- Confirmed customer saw immediate improvement (p95 -> ~200ms, 5xx -> 0.6%).

Proposed immediate next steps (24-72h):
1) Network & Infra: schedule configuration rollback or scoped config change for firewall cluster (owner: Vanessa). ETA: 48h.
2) Engineering: implement test harness for MTU/regression tests and add a canary for stateful-reassembly config pushes (owner: Soojin). ETA: 72h.
3) CS/Revenue: propose customer credit and draft joint postmortem call with BrightForge (owner: Marissa). CS to propose credit within 24h.
4) Partnerships: engage cloud provider network ops to validate peering asymmetry and confirm permanent routing plan (owner: Jon).

Attachments: SLO-runbook.docx, brightforge-pcap-sample.pcap
Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NET-4721
